```
/// Updates the rollout configuration for a specific capability.
pub async fn set_capability_rollout(rollout: CapabilityRollout) -> Result<CapabilityConfigDoc> {
  let mut config = get_capability_config().await?;

  // Find and update existing, or add new
  let existing_idx = config
    .fields
    .capabilities
    .iter()
    .position(|c| c.capability == rollout.capability);

  match existing_idx {
    Some(idx) => config.fields.capabilities[idx] = rollout,
    None => config.fields.capabilities.push(rollout),
  }

  DB.config.upsert_document(config.clone()).await?;

  // Invalidate the capability config cache
  crate::v2::capabilities::invalidate_capability_config_cache().await;

  Ok(config)
}

// ============================================================================
// User Groups functions
// ============================================================================

/// Sets the groups for a user.
pub async fn set_user_groups(id: &str, groups: Vec<String>) -> Result<User> {
  let original = get_user(id).await?;
  if let Some(mut user) = original {
    let original_user = user.clone();
    user.fields.groups = groups;
    let result = DB.users.patch_document_safe(&original_user, &user).await?;
    invalidate_user_cache(id).await;
    return Ok(result);
  }
  Err(anyhow!("Can't find user"))
}

/// Gets a summary of all groups and user counts.
pub async fn get_groups_summary() -> Result<Vec<GroupSummary>> {
  let users = get_all_users().await?;
  let mut group_counts: std::collections::HashMap<String, usize> = std::collections::HashMap::new();

  for user in users {
    for group in user.fields.groups {
      *group_counts.entry(group).or_insert(0) += 1;
    }
  }

  let mut summaries: Vec<GroupSummary> = group_counts
    .into_iter()
    .map(|(name, user_count)| GroupSummary { name, user_count })
    .collect();

  summaries.sort_by(|a, b| a.name.cmp(&b.name));
  Ok(summaries)
}

/// Summary of a group including user count.
#[derive(serde::Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct GroupSummary {
  pub name: String,
  pub user_count: usize,
}

// ============================================================================
// Family Group functions
// ============================================================================

/// Sets or clears a user's family_group_id.
pub async fn set_user_family_group(
  user_id: &ViewTypedId<UserId>,
  group_id: Option<&ViewTypedId<FamilyGroupId>>,
) -> std::result::Result<(), UserError> {
  let user = DB
    .users
    .get_document(user_id.as_str())
    .await?
    .ok_or_else(|| UserError::NotFound(user_id.as_str().to_string()))?;

  let mut updated = user.clone();
  updated.fields.family_group_id = group_id.cloned();

  DB.users.patch_document(&user, &updated).await?;
  invalidate_user_cache(user_id.as_str()).await;

  Ok(())
}

// ============================================================================
// Connected Fencers functions
// ============================================================================

/// Gets all unique connected fencer USAF IDs across all users.
/// Returns a set of USAF IDs (extracted from view format `f.u.xxx`).
/// Fencers with non-USAF IDs (e.g., database IDs) are skipped.
pub async fn get_all_connected_fencer_ids() -> Result<std::collections::HashSet<u32>> {
  let users = get_all_users().await?;
  let mut fencer_ids = std::collections::HashSet::new();

  for user in users {
    for tracked in user.fields.tracked_fencers {
      if let Some(usaf_id) = tracked.fencer_id.usaf_id() {
        fencer_ids.insert(usaf_id);
      }
    }
  }

  Ok(fencer_ids)
}

/// Connected fencer USAF ids plus each fencer's shared British Fencing
/// licence, when one is set. One licence per fencer: the value is a
/// property of the fencer, not a per-account assertion, so this cannot
/// return two licences for the same id.
pub async fn get_all_connected_fencer_ids_and_licences()
-> Result<(std::collections::HashSet<u32>, Vec<(u32, String)>)> {
  let fencer_ids = get_all_connected_fencer_ids().await?;
  let licences = crate::fencer_licence::repository::list_all(&DB.fencer_british_licences).await?;
  let mut pairs = Vec::new();
  for doc in licences {
    let Some(usaf_id) = doc.fields.fencer_id.usaf_id() else {
      continue;
    };
    if !fencer_ids.contains(&usaf_id) {
      continue;
    }
    let Some(membership_id) = doc.fields.membership_id else {
      continue;
    };
    pairs.push((usaf_id, membership_id));
  }
  Ok((fencer_ids, pairs))
}

/// Gets one user's own connected fencer USAF IDs (the fencers this account
/// tracks). Unlike [`get_all_connected_fencer_ids`], which unions every user
/// in the database and exists solely for admin/background jobs that
/// intentionally operate over the whole population, this is the
/// account-scoped lookup for user-facing (authenticated) request handlers.
pub fn get_connected_fencer_ids_for_user(user: &User) -> std::collections::HashSet<u32> {
  user
    .fields
    .tracked_fencers
    .iter()
    .filter_map(|tracked| tracked.fencer_id.usaf_id())
    .collect()
}
```

```
//! v3 REST API for user-owned writes that need their own validation rather
//! than the generic `PATCH /api/v2/user/me` json-patch path — currently just
//! the British Fencing membership id on a tracked fencer. See
//! `docs/design-docs/british-fencing-rankings-as-a-standings-source.md`,
//! "Where the membership id lives", for why this route exists instead of a
//! json-patch op on `/trackedFencers`.

pub mod rest {
  use std::str::FromStr;

  use axum::extract::Path;
  use axum::http::StatusCode;
  use axum::{Extension, Json};
  use ids::{FencerId, TypedId};
  use routez::RoutezRouter;
  use serde::Deserialize;
  use thiserror::Error;

  use crate::auth::AuthenticatedUser;
  use crate::share::is_connected_fencer;
  use crate::v2::user::set_tracked_fencer_british_fencing_licence;

  /// Mirrors the design doc: "rejects anything that is not 1-32 characters".
  const MAX_MEMBERSHIP_ID_LEN: usize = 32;

  #[derive(Debug, Error)]
  pub enum UserApiError {
    #[error("Fencer is not a connected fencer for this user")]
    FencerNotTracked,
    #[error("Invalid fencer id")]
    InvalidFencerId,
    #[error("British Fencing membership id must be 1-32 characters")]
    InvalidMembershipId,
    #[error(transparent)]
    Database(#[from] anyhow::Error),
  }

  routez::error_into_response! {
    UserApiError, err,
    log = "User API error",
    UserApiError::FencerNotTracked => StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, err.to_string();
    UserApiError::InvalidFencerId => StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, err.to_string();
    UserApiError::InvalidMembershipId => StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, err.to_string();
    UserApiError::Database(_) => StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, "Internal server error";
  }

  type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, UserApiError>;

  /// Router mounted at `/user` in the protected v3 router.
  pub fn router() -> RoutezRouter {
    RoutezRouter::new().route_put(
      "/tracked-fencers/{fencer_id}/british-fencing-membership",
      set_british_fencing_membership,
    )
  }

  #[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
  #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
  struct SetBritishFencingMembershipRequest {
    #[serde(default)]
    membership_id: Option<String>,
  }

  /// Normalizes a raw `membershipId` request value: `None`, an empty string,
  /// or a whitespace-only string all clear the licence (`Ok(None)`);
  /// otherwise the trimmed value is returned if it is 1-32 characters (by
  /// `chars().count()`, not byte length), and rejected above that.
  fn normalize_membership_id(raw: Option<String>) -> Result<Option<String>> {
    let Some(raw) = raw else {
      return Ok(None);
    };
    let trimmed = raw.trim();
    if trimmed.is_empty() {
      Ok(None)
    } else if trimmed.chars().count() > MAX_MEMBERSHIP_ID_LEN {
      Err(UserApiError::InvalidMembershipId)
    } else {
      Ok(Some(trimmed.to_string()))
    }
  }

  /// Sets or clears the caller's British Fencing membership id for one of
  /// their own tracked fencers. `membershipId: null` (or an empty /
  /// whitespace-only string) clears it; otherwise the trimmed value must be
  /// 1-32 characters.
  async fn set_british_fencing_membership(
    Extension(auth): Extension<AuthenticatedUser>,
    Path(fencer_id): Path<String>,
    Json(request): Json<SetBritishFencingMembershipRequest>,
  ) -> Result<StatusCode> {
    let fencer_id =
      TypedId::<FencerId>::from_str(&fencer_id).map_err(|_| UserApiError::InvalidFencerId)?;

    if !is_connected_fencer(&auth.user.fields.tracked_fencers, &fencer_id) {
      return Err(UserApiError::FencerNotTracked);
    }

    let licence = normalize_membership_id(request.membership_id)?;

    let fencer_id_str = fencer_id.to_view_string();
    let tracked =
      set_tracked_fencer_british_fencing_licence(&auth.user.id, &fencer_id_str, licence).await?;
    if !tracked {
      return Err(UserApiError::FencerNotTracked);
    }

    Ok(StatusCode::NO_CONTENT)
  }

  #[cfg(test)]
  mod tests {
    use axum::response::IntoResponse;

    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn fencer_not_tracked_is_not_found() {
      let response = UserApiError::FencerNotTracked.into_response();
      assert_eq!(response.status(), StatusCode::NOT_FOUND);
    }

    #[test]
    fn invalid_fencer_id_is_bad_request() {
      let response = UserApiError::InvalidFencerId.into_response();
      assert_eq!(response.status(), StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);
    }

    #[test]
    fn invalid_membership_id_is_bad_request() {
      let response = UserApiError::InvalidMembershipId.into_response();
      assert_eq!(response.status(), StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);
    }

    #[test]
    fn database_error_is_internal_server_error() {
      let response = UserApiError::Database(anyhow::anyhow!("boom")).into_response();
      assert_eq!(response.status(), StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR);
    }

    #[test]
    fn normalize_none_clears() {
      assert_eq!(normalize_membership_id(None).unwrap(), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn normalize_whitespace_only_clears() {
      assert_eq!(
        normalize_membership_id(Some("   ".to_string())).unwrap(),
        None
      );
    }

    #[test]
    fn normalize_trims() {
      assert_eq!(
        normalize_membership_id(Some(" 142013 ".to_string())).unwrap(),
        Some("142013".to_string())
      );
    }

    #[test]
    fn normalize_accepts_exactly_max_length() {
      let value = "a".repeat(MAX_MEMBERSHIP_ID_LEN);
      assert_eq!(
        normalize_membership_id(Some(value.clone())).unwrap(),
        Some(value)
      );
    }

    #[test]
    fn normalize_rejects_over_max_length() {
      let value = "a".repeat(MAX_MEMBERSHIP_ID_LEN + 1);
      assert!(matches!(
        normalize_membership_id(Some(value)),
        Err(UserApiError::InvalidMembershipId)
      ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn normalize_rejects_over_max_length_multibyte_chars() {
      // 33 multi-byte characters: over the 32-char limit by `chars().count()`
      // even though the check must not use byte length (each char is >1 byte).
      let value = "é".repeat(MAX_MEMBERSHIP_ID_LEN + 1);
      assert!(matches!(
        normalize_membership_id(Some(value)),
        Err(UserApiError::InvalidMembershipId)
      ));
    }
  }
}
```

```
/// Mints a Flunge-owned typed standing id.
///
/// The opaque id preserves the scope and classifier: `nat-{code}` for national
/// standings, `r{regionId}-{code}` for genuine per-region standings,
/// `rs-{code}` for `RegionalShared` (Division) categories, `uni-{code}`
/// for Unified standings, and `gb-{code}` for British Fencing standings. As a
/// derived, Flunge-owned record it uses the database system, yielding view
/// ids such as `s.d.nat-SRMF` and `s.d.r3-JRME`.
pub(crate) fn build_standing_key(
  scope: StandingScope,
  region_id: Option<u8>,
  code: &str,
) -> TypedId<StandingId> {
  let opaque_id = match (scope, region_id) {
    (StandingScope::National, _) => format!("nat-{code}"),
    (StandingScope::Regional, Some(region_id)) => format!("r{region_id}-{code}"),
    (StandingScope::Regional, None) => format!("rs-{code}"),
    (StandingScope::Unified, _) => format!("uni-{code}"),
    (StandingScope::British, _) => format!("gb-{code}"),
  };
  TypedId::<StandingId>::new_with_system(&opaque_id, System::Database)
}

/// Parses and validates a server-minted standing key.
///
/// A syntactically valid `StandingId` alone is not sufficient: this endpoint
/// only accepts the database-owned `nat-`, `r{region}-`, `rs-`, `uni-`, and
/// `gb-` forms that [`build_standing_key`] creates.
pub(crate) fn parse_standing_key(raw: &str) -> Result<TypedId<StandingId>> {
  let key = parse_typed_id::<StandingId>(raw, "standing")
    .map_err(|_| StandingsError::InvalidStandingKey(raw.to_string()))?;
  if key.system() != &System::Database {
    return Err(StandingsError::InvalidStandingKey(raw.to_string()));
  }

  let valid = match key.as_str().split_once('-') {
    Some(("nat", classifier))
    | Some(("rs", classifier))
    | Some(("uni", classifier))
    | Some(("gb", classifier)) => RecognizedClassifier::from_code(classifier).is_some(),
    Some((region, classifier)) => {
      region
        .strip_prefix('r')
        .and_then(|region| region.parse::<u8>().ok())
        .is_some_and(|region| region > 0)
        && RecognizedClassifier::from_code(classifier).is_some()
    }
    None => false,
  };
  if valid {
    Ok(key)
  } else {
    Err(StandingsError::InvalidStandingKey(raw.to_string()))
  }
}

  pub(crate) code: String,
```
