#[test]
fn source_freshness_flatten_matches_prior_unified_wire_shape() {
  // Regression for the `SourceFreshness` extraction: `sourceUpdatedAt`/
  // `fetchedAt`/`isStale` used to be flat fields directly on
  // `UnifiedStandingItemMetadata`; they are now `#[serde(flatten)]`ed from a
  // nested `SourceFreshness`, and the wire keys must be byte-for-byte
  // unchanged. `points_floor`/`eligibility` stay `None` here deliberately, so
  // the object contains exactly the five keys this asserts -- no stray key
  // survives an accidental un-skip.
  let metadata = UnifiedStandingItemMetadata {
    freshness: SourceFreshness {
      source_updated_at: Some(1700000000),
      fetched_at: Some(1700000100),
      is_stale: Some(false),
    },
    list_code: Some("CDTWS".to_string()),
    is_new: true,
    points_floor: None,
    eligibility: None,
    counted: Vec::new(),
  };

  let value = serde_json::to_value(&metadata).unwrap();
  assert_eq!(value["sourceUpdatedAt"], 1700000000);
  assert_eq!(value["fetchedAt"], 1700000100);
  assert_eq!(value["isStale"], false);
  assert_eq!(value["listCode"], "CDTWS");
  assert_eq!(value["isNew"], true);
  assert_eq!(value.as_object().unwrap().len(), 5);
}

fn british_row(
  licence: &str,
  position: u32,
  total_points: i64,
) -> british_fencing::BritishRankingRow {
  british_fencing::BritishRankingRow {
    rank: model_common::Rank {
      position,
      is_tied: false,
    },
    name: "Fencer, Test".to_string(),
    year_of_birth: None,
    club: None,
    licence: licence.to_string(),
    total_points,
    domestic: british_fencing::BritishBucketTotal {
      points: total_points,
      counted_events: 1,
    },
    international: british_fencing::BritishBucketTotal {
      points: 0,
      counted_events: 0,
    },
    results: Vec::new(),
    counted_selection: Default::default(),
  }
}

fn british_table(
  rows: Vec<british_fencing::BritishRankingRow>,
  fetched_at: chrono::DateTime<Utc>,
) -> british_fencing::BritishRankingTable {
  british_fencing::BritishRankingTable {
    table_id: "cadet-womens-sabre".to_string(),
    classifier: RecognizedClassifier::from_code("CDTWS").unwrap(),
    source_title: "Cadet Women's Sabre".to_string(),
    source_updated_at: fetched_at - Duration::hours(2),
    fetched_at,
    events: Vec::new(),
    rows,
  }
}

fn british_event(
  name: &str,
  date: &str,
  kind: british_fencing::BritishEventKind,
) -> british_fencing::BritishRankingEvent {
  british_fencing::BritishRankingEvent {
    name: name.to_string(),
    date: NaiveDate::parse_from_str(date, "%Y-%m-%d").unwrap(),
    kind,
  }
}

  event_index: usize,

) -> british_fencing::BritishRankingResult {

  }
}

#[test]
fn british_composition_projects_source_buckets_and_ambiguity() {
  let mut table = british_table(vec![], Utc::now());
  table.events = vec![
    british_event(
      "London Open",
      "2026-01-10",
      british_fencing::BritishEventKind::Domestic,
    ),
    british_event(
      "Birmingham Open",
      "2026-02-10",
      british_fencing::BritishEventKind::Domestic,
    ),
    british_event(
      "European Cup",
      "2026-03-10",
      british_fencing::BritishEventKind::International,
    ),
  ];
  let mut row = british_row("142013", 12, 125);
  row.domestic = british_fencing::BritishBucketTotal {
    points: 50,
    counted_events: 1,
  };
  row.international = british_fencing::BritishBucketTotal {
    points: 75,
    counted_events: 1,
  };
  row.results = vec![
    british_result(0, 3, 50),
    british_result(1, 8, 30),
    british_result(2, 5, 75),
  ];
  row.counted_selection = british_fencing::BritishCountedSelection {
    domestic_event_indexes: vec![0],
    international_event_indexes: vec![2],
    is_ambiguous: true,
  };

  let body = resolve_british_composition_body(&table, &row, 125.0);
  let StandingCompositionBody::Complete {
    source,
    rule,
    counted_total,
    counted,
    excluded,
    counted_selection_ambiguous,
    excluded_availability,
    ..
  } = body
  else {
    panic!("expected complete British composition");
  };

  assert!(matches!(
    source,
    CompositionSource::BritishFencingLiveRanking
  ));
  assert!(matches!(
    rule,
    CountingRule::DomesticInternationalSplit {
      domestic_counted: 1,
      international_counted: 1,
      ..
    }
  ));
  assert_eq!(counted_total, 125.0);
  assert_eq!(
    counted.iter().map(|entry| entry.bucket).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    vec![
      Some(CompositionEntryBucket::Domestic),
      Some(CompositionEntryBucket::International),
    ]
  );
  assert_eq!(excluded.len(), 1);
  assert_eq!(
    excluded[0]
      .excluded_reason
      .as_ref()
      .map(|reason| serde_json::to_value(reason).unwrap()),
    Some(serde_json::json!("displacedByBestN"))
  );
  assert_eq!(counted_selection_ambiguous, Some(true));
  assert!(matches!(
    excluded_availability,
    ExcludedAvailability::Complete
  ));
}

#[test]
fn british_composition_refuses_when_the_counted_selection_index_count_disagrees_with_published_counts()
 {
  let mut table = british_table(vec![], Utc::now());
  table.events = vec![british_event(
    "London Open",
    "2026-01-10",
    british_fencing::BritishEventKind::Domestic,
  )];
  let mut row = british_row("142013", 12, 50);
  row.results = vec![british_result(0, 3, 50)];
  // Published counted_events says 1 domestic, but the selection carries none --
  // a manually-corrupt payload the ingestion validator should never produce.
  row.counted_selection.domestic_event_indexes = vec![];

  assert!(matches!(
    resolve_british_composition_body(&table, &row, 50.0),
    StandingCompositionBody::Unavailable {
      reason: UnavailableReason::UpstreamUnavailable
    }
  ));
}

#[test]

#[test]
fn british_standing_item_for_row_reports_scope_key_and_entrant_count() {
  let table = british_table(
    vec![
      british_row("142013", 12, 37210),
      british_row("999999", 1, 50000),
    ],
    Utc::now(),
  );

  assert_eq!(item.scope, StandingScope::British);
  assert_eq!(item.key.to_string(), "s.d.gb-CDTWS");
  assert_eq!(item.region_id, None);
  assert_eq!(item.rank.position, 12);
  assert_eq!(item.points, Some(37210.0));
  // The parsed row count, not the highest rank on a tied field -- see the
  // design doc's "A chip's field size must be the parsed row count, never
  // the highest rank."
  assert_eq!(item.entrants, Some(2));
  assert!(item.unified.is_none());
}

#[test]
fn may_resolve_british_licence_when_the_caller_tracks_the_fencer() {
  let fencer_id = TypedId::<FencerId>::usaf("100344622");
  let tracked = vec![TrackedFencer {
    fencer_id: fencer_id.clone(),
    results_backfill: Default::default(),
    british_fencing_licence: None,
  }];
  assert!(may_resolve_british_licence(&tracked, &fencer_id));
}

#[test]
fn may_resolve_british_licence_is_false_when_the_fencer_is_not_tracked() {
  let tracked = vec![TrackedFencer {
    fencer_id: TypedId::<FencerId>::usaf("999"),
    results_backfill: Default::default(),
    british_fencing_licence: None,
  }];
  assert!(!may_resolve_british_licence(
    &tracked,
    &TypedId::<FencerId>::usaf("100344622")
  ));
}

#[test]
fn a_tracker_who_set_nothing_still_passes_the_shared_licence_gate() {
  // Two accounts tracking the same fencer share the sidecar licence.
  // The gate is "does this viewing context track the fencer", not "did
  // this account type the number".
  let fencer_id = TypedId::<FencerId>::usaf("100344622");
  let tracked = vec![TrackedFencer {
    fencer_id: fencer_id.clone(),
    results_backfill: Default::default(),
    british_fencing_licence: None,
  }];
  assert!(may_resolve_british_licence(&tracked, &fencer_id));
}

#[test]
fn fencer_standings_router_still_registers_the_fencer_standings_route() {
  // Regression for the `optional_auth_middleware` layering refactor: the
  // route must survive being split into its own sub-router and merged back.
  assert!(super::super::rest::router().routes().iter().any(|route| {
    route.method == axum::http::Method::GET && route.path == "/fencer/{fencer_id}"
  }));
}

//! The additive standings movement and trajectory read surface.

use std::collections::HashMap;

use axum::Json;
use axum::extract::{Extension, Path, Query};
use chrono::{DateTime, Duration, Utc};
use ids::{FencerId, StandingId, TypedId};
use model_common::Rank;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use standings_history::{
  MovementSummary, ReceiptOutcome, SnapshotRunReceiptFields, StandingSnapshotProjection, repository,
};
use tracing::warn;

use crate::auth::AuthenticatedUser;
use crate::db::DB;
use crate::standings_history::{SCHEDULE, read_movement, slot_run_id_from};
use crate::view::ids::parse_typed_id;

use super::{
  ClassifierInfo, FencerStandingsResponse, Result, StandingScope, StandingsError,
  get_fencer_standings, licence_for_fencer, parse_standing_key,
};

/// Projected history for a single standing. The contributor arrays live in
/// Cosmos for a later explain-why surface, but are intentionally never read
/// by this graph endpoint.
#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct StandingHistoryResponse {
  fencer_id: TypedId<FencerId>,
  standing_key: TypedId<StandingId>,
  scope: StandingScope,
  classifier: ClassifierInfo,
  window_days: u32,
  points: Vec<StandingHistoryPoint>,
  gaps: Vec<StandingHistoryGap>,
  #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
  movement: Option<MovementSummary>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct StandingHistoryPoint {
  run_id: String,
  captured_at: DateTime<Utc>,
  rank: Rank,
  #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
  points: Option<f32>,
  #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
  entrants: Option<usize>,
  source_stale: bool,
  #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
  composition_state: Option<String>,
  #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
  composition_reason: Option<String>,
}

impl From<StandingSnapshotProjection> for StandingHistoryPoint {
  fn from(snapshot: StandingSnapshotProjection) -> Self {
    Self {
      run_id: snapshot.run_id,
      captured_at: snapshot.captured_at,
      rank: snapshot.rank,
      points: snapshot.points,
      entrants: snapshot.entrants,
      source_stale: snapshot.source.stale,
      composition_state: snapshot.composition_state,
      composition_reason: snapshot.composition_reason,
    }
  }
}

#[derive(Debug, Serialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct StandingHistoryGap {
  pub(crate) run_id: String,
  pub(crate) kind: StandingHistoryGapKind,
}

#[derive(Debug, Serialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub enum StandingHistoryGapKind {
  CaptureFailed,
  NotAttempted,
  StandingAbsent,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
pub struct StandingHistoryQuery {
  pub(crate) days: Option<u32>,
}

pub(crate) const DEFAULT_HISTORY_WINDOW_DAYS: u32 = 180;

/// Attaches the task-produced summaries with one `HGET` for the whole
/// response. A Redis miss or malformed cache value deliberately degrades to
/// no indicator instead of letting derived state make standings unavailable.
pub(crate) async fn attach_movement(response: FencerStandingsResponse) -> FencerStandingsResponse {
  match read_movement(&response.fencer_id.to_string()).await {
    Ok(movement) => apply_movement(response, movement),
    Err(error) => {
      warn!(
        fencer_id = %response.fencer_id,
        ?error,
        "Failed to read standings movement summaries; serving standings without movement"
      );
      response
    }
  }
}

/// Matches precomputed summaries onto the items they belong to. Keys with no
/// summary keep `movement: None`; extra hash entries that do not match an
/// item are dropped. Pure so owner and share can share one implementation
/// without a Redis fake.
pub(crate) fn apply_movement(
  mut response: FencerStandingsResponse,
  mut movement: HashMap<String, MovementSummary>,
) -> FencerStandingsResponse {
  for standing in &mut response.standings {
    standing.movement = movement.remove(&standing.key.to_string());
  }
  response
}

/// Returns the projected observation series used by the standing trajectory
/// graph. The current-standing lookup intentionally matches the composition
/// route: malformed keys are rejected before reads, while a valid key absent
/// from this fencer's current standings is a 404.
#[axum::debug_handler]
pub async fn get_standing_history_handler(
  Path((raw_fencer_id, raw_standing_key)): Path<(String, String)>,
  Query(query): Query<StandingHistoryQuery>,
  authed: Option<Extension<AuthenticatedUser>>,
) -> Result<Json<StandingHistoryResponse>> {
  let fencer_id = parse_typed_id::<FencerId>(&raw_fencer_id, "fencer")?;
  let standing_key = parse_standing_key(&raw_standing_key)?;
  let british_licence = authed.and_then(|Extension(authed)| {
    licence_for_fencer(&authed.user.fields.tracked_fencers, &fencer_id)
  });
  let standing = get_fencer_standings(fencer_id.clone(), british_licence.as_deref())
    .await?
    .standings
    .into_iter()
    .find(|standing| standing.key == standing_key)
    .ok_or_else(|| StandingsError::StandingNotFound(standing_key.to_string()))?;

  let window_days = history_window_days(
    query.days,
    flunge_config::CONF.standings_history.retention_days,
  );
  let now = Utc::now();
  let since = now - Duration::days(i64::from(window_days));
  let snapshots = repository::list_standing_snapshots_in_window(
    &DB.standings_history_snapshots,
    &fencer_id.to_string(),
    &standing_key.to_string(),
    since,
  )
  .await
  .map_err(|error| StandingsError::Database(error.to_string()))?;
  let receipts = repository::list_receipts_in_window(
    &DB.standings_history_receipts,
    &fencer_id.to_string(),
    since,
  )
  .await
  .map_err(|error| StandingsError::Database(error.to_string()))?
  .into_iter()
  .map(|receipt| receipt.fields)
  .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  let slots = cron_schedule::execution_times_in_window(SCHEDULE, since, now)
    .ok_or_else(|| StandingsError::Database("invalid standings history schedule".to_string()))?;

  let mut points = snapshots
    .into_iter()
    .map(StandingHistoryPoint::from)
    .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  points.sort_by_key(|point| point.captured_at);
  let movement = match read_movement(&fencer_id.to_string()).await {
    Ok(mut movement) => movement.remove(&standing_key.to_string()),
    Err(error) => {
      warn!(
        %fencer_id,
        ?error,
        "Failed to read standings movement summary for history response"
      );
      None
    }
  };

  Ok(Json(StandingHistoryResponse {
    fencer_id,
    standing_key,
    scope: standing.scope,
    classifier: standing.classifier,
    window_days,
    points,
    gaps: history_gaps(slots, &receipts, standing.key.as_str()),
    movement,
  }))
}

pub(crate) fn history_window_days(days: Option<u32>, retention_days: u32) -> u32 {
  days
    .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_HISTORY_WINDOW_DAYS)
    .clamp(1, retention_days)
}

pub(crate) fn history_gaps(
  slots: Vec<DateTime<Utc>>,
  receipts: &[SnapshotRunReceiptFields],
  standing_key: &str,
) -> Vec<StandingHistoryGap> {
  slots
    .into_iter()
    .filter_map(|slot| {
      let run_id = slot_run_id_from(slot);
      let kind = match receipts.iter().find(|receipt| receipt.run_id == run_id) {
        None => StandingHistoryGapKind::NotAttempted,
        Some(SnapshotRunReceiptFields {
          outcome: ReceiptOutcome::Failed { .. },
          ..
        }) => StandingHistoryGapKind::CaptureFailed,
        Some(SnapshotRunReceiptFields {
          outcome: ReceiptOutcome::Succeeded { standing_keys },
          ..
        }) if !standing_keys.iter().any(|key| key == standing_key) => {
          StandingHistoryGapKind::StandingAbsent
        }
        Some(_) => return None,
      };
      Some(StandingHistoryGap { run_id, kind })
    })
    .collect()
}
```

+//! Shared British Fencing membership id (their "Licence") for a fencer.
+//!
+//! This is a fact about the fencer, not a private annotation on a user
+//! account: anyone who tracks the fencer may set or correct it, last write
+//! wins, and every other tracker sees the same value. It lives in its own
+//! Cosmos collection, keyed by fencer id, so the fencer-refresh path that
+//! rewrites scraper-owned `FencerFields` is structurally unable to touch it.
+//!
+//! The repository operates over a `cosmos::Collection<FencerLicenceFields>`
+//! passed in by the caller, so this crate never depends on `blob`.
+
+pub mod migrate;
+pub mod model;
+pub mod repository;
+
+pub use migrate::{MigrationDecision, MigrationPlan, PerUserAssertion, plan_migration};
+pub use model::FencerLicenceFields;
+pub use repository::document_id;
```

+//! Pure planner for lifting per-user British Fencing licence assertions
+//! onto the shared fencer record.
+//!
+//! Where exactly one distinct membership id exists across every user
+//! tracking a fencer, that value is adopted. Where two or more users
+//! asserted *different* ids for the same fencer, the shared record is left
+//! unset — the planner never guesses. Callers log the conflict by fencer
+//! id and distinct-count only; they must never log the membership ids
+//! themselves.
+
+use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
+
+use ids::{FencerId, TypedId, UserId};
+
+/// One user's stored assertion of a British Fencing membership id for a
+/// fencer they track. `membership_id` is the already-trimmed stored value.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub struct PerUserAssertion {
+  pub user_id: TypedId<UserId>,
+  pub fencer_id: TypedId<FencerId>,
+  pub membership_id: String,
+}
+
+/// What to do for one fencer that had at least one per-user assertion.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum MigrationDecision {
+  /// Every asserting user agreed (or only one asserted). Write this value
+  /// as the shared licence, attributed to `set_by`.
+  Adopt {
+    fencer_id: TypedId<FencerId>,
+    membership_id: String,
+    set_by: TypedId<UserId>,
+  },
+  /// Two or more distinct membership ids were asserted. Leave the shared
+  /// licence unset. `distinct_count` is the number of different ids, never
+  /// the ids themselves.
+  Conflict {
+    fencer_id: TypedId<FencerId>,
+    distinct_count: usize,
+  },
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
+pub struct MigrationPlan {
+  pub decisions: Vec<MigrationDecision>,
+}
+
+impl MigrationPlan {
+  pub fn adopted_count(&self) -> usize {
+    self
+      .decisions
+      .iter()
+      .filter(|d| matches!(d, MigrationDecision::Adopt { .. }))
+      .count()
+  }
+
+  pub fn conflicted_count(&self) -> usize {
+    self
+      .decisions
+      .iter()
+      .filter(|d| matches!(d, MigrationDecision::Conflict { .. }))
+      .count()
+  }
+}
+
+/// Groups per-user assertions by fencer and decides adopt-vs-conflict for
+/// each. Fencers with no assertions are omitted. Adopted `set_by` is the
+/// lexicographically-smallest asserting user id so two replicas planning
+/// the same input produce the same provenance.
+pub fn plan_migration(assertions: &[PerUserAssertion]) -> MigrationPlan {
+  let mut by_fencer: HashMap<TypedId<FencerId>, HashMap<String, HashSet<TypedId<UserId>>>> =
+    HashMap::new();
+  for assertion in assertions {
+    by_fencer
+      .entry(assertion.fencer_id.clone())
+      .or_default()
+      .entry(assertion.membership_id.clone())
+      .or_default()
+      .insert(assertion.user_id.clone());
+  }
+
+  let mut decisions = Vec::with_capacity(by_fencer.len());
+  for (fencer_id, licences) in by_fencer {
+    match licences.len() {
+      0 => {}
+      1 => {
+        let (membership_id, users) = licences.into_iter().next().unwrap();
+        let mut users: Vec<_> = users.into_iter().collect();
+        users.sort_by_key(|user| user.to_string());
+        let set_by = users
+          .into_iter()
+          .next()
+          .expect("at least one asserting user");
+        decisions.push(MigrationDecision::Adopt {
+          fencer_id,
+          membership_id,
+          set_by,
+        });
+      }
+      distinct_count => {
+        decisions.push(MigrationDecision::Conflict {
+          fencer_id,
+          distinct_count,
+        });
+      }
+    }
+  }
+  MigrationPlan { decisions }
+}

pub enum MigrationDecision {

  /// as the shared licence, attributed to `set_by`.

    fencer_id: TypedId<FencerId>,
    membership_id: String,

pub struct MigrationPlan {
  pub decisions: Vec<MigrationDecision>,

impl MigrationPlan {

    self

      .filter(|d| matches!(d, MigrationDecision::Adopt { .. }))
      .count()

  pub fn conflicted_count(&self) -> usize {

      .iter()
      .filter(|d| matches!(d, MigrationDecision::Conflict { .. }))
      .count()
  }
}

/// Groups per-user assertions by fencer and decides adopt-vs-conflict for
/// each. Fencers with no assertions are omitted. Adopted `set_by` is the
/// lexicographically-smallest asserting user id so two replicas planning
/// the same input produce the same provenance.
pub fn plan_migration(assertions: &[PerUserAssertion]) -> MigrationPlan {
  let mut by_fencer: HashMap<TypedId<FencerId>, HashMap<String, HashSet<TypedId<UserId>>>> =
    HashMap::new();

    by_fencer
      .entry(assertion.fencer_id.clone())
      .or_default()
      .entry(assertion.membership_id.clone())
      .or_default()
      .insert(assertion.user_id.clone());
  }

  let mut decisions = Vec::with_capacity(by_fencer.len());
  for (fencer_id, licences) in by_fencer {
    match licences.len() {
      0 => {}
      1 => {
        let (membership_id, users) = licences.into_iter().next().unwrap();

          fencer_id,
          membership_id,
          set_by,
        });
      }
      distinct_count => {
        decisions.push(MigrationDecision::Conflict {
          fencer_id,
          distinct_count,
        });
      }
    }
  }

@@ -0,0 +1,121 @@
+//! Database operations for the shared fencer-licence collection.
+//!
+//! These functions operate over a `cosmos::Collection<FencerLicenceFields>`
+//! supplied by the caller (`blob` wires it into `DbClient`). Passing the
+//! collection in keeps this crate free of any dependency on `blob`.
+
+use std::collections::HashMap;
+
+use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
+use cosmos::{Collection, Select, SelectBuilder, SqlFilter, id_in};
+use ids::{FencerId, Identified, TypedId, UserId};
+
+use crate::model::FencerLicenceFields;
+
+/// Stable storage key for one fencer's shared licence. Distinct from the
+/// fencers-collection document id, so a fencer refresh that patches
+/// `FencerFields` cannot address this record.
+pub fn document_id(fencer_id: &TypedId<FencerId>) -> String {
+  format!("bfl-{}", fencer_id)
+}
+
+/// Loads the shared licence document for `fencer_id`, if one has ever been
+/// written (including an explicit clear).
+pub async fn get(
+  licences: &Collection<FencerLicenceFields>,
+  fencer_id: &TypedId<FencerId>,
+) -> anyhow::Result<Option<Identified<FencerLicenceFields>>> {
+  licences.get_document(&document_id(fencer_id)).await
+}
+
+/// The current membership id, or `None` if unset, cleared, or never written.
+pub async fn get_membership_id(
+  licences: &Collection<FencerLicenceFields>,
+  fencer_id: &TypedId<FencerId>,
+) -> anyhow::Result<Option<String>> {
+  Ok(
+    get(licences, fencer_id)
+      .await?
+      .and_then(|doc| doc.fields.membership_id),
+  )
+}
+
+struct ByFencerIdsFilter {
+  document_ids: Vec<String>,
+}
+
+impl SqlFilter for ByFencerIdsFilter {
+  fn to_select(&self) -> anyhow::Result<Select> {
+    Ok(
+      SelectBuilder::all()
+        .condition(id_in(&self.document_ids)?)
+        .build()?,
+    )
+  }
+}
+
+/// Loads the current membership id for every fencer in `fencer_ids` in a
+/// single query, keyed by fencer id. A fencer with no shared record (never
+/// written) is simply absent from the map rather than mapped to `None`.
+pub async fn get_membership_ids(
+  licences: &Collection<FencerLicenceFields>,
+  fencer_ids: &[TypedId<FencerId>],
+) -> anyhow::Result<HashMap<TypedId<FencerId>, Option<String>>> {
+  if fencer_ids.is_empty() {
+    return Ok(HashMap::new());
+  }
+  let document_ids = fencer_ids.iter().map(document_id).collect();
+  let docs = licences
+    .list_documents_filtered(ByFencerIdsFilter { document_ids })
+    .await?;
+  Ok(
+    docs
+      .into_iter()
+      .map(|doc| (doc.fields.fencer_id, doc.fields.membership_id))
+      .collect(),
+  )
+}
+
+/// Last-write-wins upsert. `membership_id: None` is an explicit clear; the
+/// document is kept so `set_by` / `set_at` remain.
+pub async fn upsert(
+  licences: &Collection<FencerLicenceFields>,
+  fencer_id: TypedId<FencerId>,

```
//! Database operations for the shared fencer-licence collection.
//!
//! These functions operate over a `cosmos::Collection<FencerLicenceFields>`
//! supplied by the caller (`blob` wires it into `DbClient`). Passing the
//! collection in keeps this crate free of any dependency on `blob`.

use std::collections::HashMap;

use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
use cosmos::{Collection, Select, SelectBuilder, SqlFilter, id_in};
use ids::{FencerId, Identified, TypedId, UserId};

use crate::model::FencerLicenceFields;

/// Stable storage key for one fencer's shared licence. Distinct from the
/// fencers-collection document id, so a fencer refresh that patches
/// `FencerFields` cannot address this record.
pub fn document_id(fencer_id: &TypedId<FencerId>) -> String {
  format!("bfl-{}", fencer_id)
}

/// Loads the shared licence document for `fencer_id`, if one has ever been
/// written (including an explicit clear).
pub async fn get(
  licences: &Collection<FencerLicenceFields>,
  fencer_id: &TypedId<FencerId>,
) -> anyhow::Result<Option<Identified<FencerLicenceFields>>> {
  licences.get_document(&document_id(fencer_id)).await
}

/// The current membership id, or `None` if unset, cleared, or never written.
pub async fn get_membership_id(
  licences: &Collection<FencerLicenceFields>,
  fencer_id: &TypedId<FencerId>,
) -> anyhow::Result<Option<String>> {
  Ok(
    get(licences, fencer_id)
      .await?
      .and_then(|doc| doc.fields.membership_id),
  )
}

struct ByFencerIdsFilter {
  document_ids: Vec<String>,
}

impl SqlFilter for ByFencerIdsFilter {
  fn to_select(&self) -> anyhow::Result<Select> {
    Ok(
      SelectBuilder::all()
        .condition(id_in(&self.document_ids)?)
        .build()?,
    )
  }
}

/// Loads the current membership id for every fencer in `fencer_ids` in a
/// single query, keyed by fencer id. A fencer with no shared record (never
/// written) is simply absent from the map rather than mapped to `None`.
pub async fn get_membership_ids(
  licences: &Collection<FencerLicenceFields>,
  fencer_ids: &[TypedId<FencerId>],
) -> anyhow::Result<HashMap<TypedId<FencerId>, Option<String>>> {
  if fencer_ids.is_empty() {
    return Ok(HashMap::new());
  }
  let document_ids = fencer_ids.iter().map(document_id).collect();
  let docs = licences
    .list_documents_filtered(ByFencerIdsFilter { document_ids })
    .await?;
  Ok(
    docs
      .into_iter()
      .map(|doc| (doc.fields.fencer_id, doc.fields.membership_id))
      .collect(),
  )
}

/// Last-write-wins upsert. `membership_id: None` is an explicit clear; the
/// document is kept so `set_by` / `set_at` remain.
pub async fn upsert(
  licences: &Collection<FencerLicenceFields>,
  fencer_id: TypedId<FencerId>,
  membership_id: Option<String>,
  set_by: TypedId<UserId>,
  set_at: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> anyhow::Result<Identified<FencerLicenceFields>> {
  let doc = Identified {
    id: document_id(&fencer_id),
    fields: FencerLicenceFields::new(fencer_id, membership_id, set_by, set_at),
    partition: Some("flunge".to_string()),
  };
  licences.upsert_document(doc).await
}

/// Every licence document. Used by standings-history capture and by
/// migration to skip fencers that already have a shared record.
pub async fn list_all(
  licences: &Collection<FencerLicenceFields>,
) -> anyhow::Result<Vec<Identified<FencerLicenceFields>>> {
  licences.list_documents().await
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
  use super::*;

  #[test]
  fn document_id_is_not_the_fencer_view_id() {
    let fencer_id = TypedId::<FencerId>::usaf("100344622");
    let id = document_id(&fencer_id);
    assert_eq!(id, "bfl-f.u.100344622");
    assert_ne!(id, fencer_id.to_string());
  }

  #[test]
  fn document_id_is_stable_for_a_given_fencer() {
    let fencer_id = TypedId::<FencerId>::usaf("100344622");
    assert_eq!(document_id(&fencer_id), document_id(&fencer_id));
  }
}

# Backend

The backend is a Rust binary in `backend/` using Axum as the web framework.

## Building

```sh
bazel build //backend:backend
```

To run it locally, the binary loads `config.toml`, `config-common.toml`, and `config-secrets.toml` by relative path from its cwd, and the `//backend:backend` target has no `data` deps for them, so run it from within `backend/` (where those files live) rather than via `bazel run`:

```sh
cd backend && ../bazel-bin/backend/backend
```

`config-secrets.toml` isn't checked in (see [`config-secrets.toml.gpg`](../backend/config-secrets.toml.gpg)); decrypt it first if it's missing from your checkout.

The backend serves at http://localhost:8080. Check http://localhost:8080/statusz for health.

## Workspace Structure

The backend is a Cargo workspace (edition 2024, resolver 3) with these member crates:

The entry point is `backend/main.rs`. It is the composition root: it assembles a `blob::startup::Extensions` from the crates layered above `blob` (today `admintasks`) and passes it to `blob::run_sync()`, which calls into `backend/blob/src/app.rs`.

## Key Dependencies

- **Web framework:** Axum 0.8
- **Async runtime:** Tokio (multi-threaded)
- **Database:** Azure Cosmos DB (`azure_data_cosmos`)
- **Caching:** Redis via `cached` crate
- **Auth:** `jsonwebtoken`
- **Scheduling:** `tokio-cron-scheduler`
- **Observability:** `tracing` with JSON output, Prometheus metrics

## API Versioning

The API has versioned modules (`v2/`, `v3/`). New work should target `v3`.
When a PR changes backend API behavior, include a related docs update in the same PR — in this file, in the matching per-area note under [`docs/backend/`](backend/) (see [Subsystem API Notes](#subsystem-api-notes)), or in a product spec. This is a team convention, not a CI gate.

## Subsystem API Notes

Per-area backend API-surface notes live under [`docs/backend/`](backend/), one file per subsystem. They were split out of this file so it can stay a small, stable conventions doc. Backend PRs that change API behavior append notes to these files; putting every note in one growing tail of this document made concurrent PRs conflict textually. Per-area files spread those appends out so logically independent PRs stop colliding.

When you change an API's behavior, add the note to the matching area file below (or to a product spec under `docs/product-specs/`).

- [Routes & operational endpoints](backend/routes.md) — route cleanup history, operational & shim endpoints, dynamic flags, OAuth state, CORS
- [Results view API](backend/results.md) — rollout observability, connected-fencer backfill, bout-backed read-path, video API, FencingTimeLive import, manual refresh
- [Fencers view API](backend/fencers.md) — `GET /api/v3/view/fencers` follow/notify + listing
- [Standings view API](backend/standings.md) — cached enriched-view read path, connected-fencer standings endpoint
- [Ratings view API](backend/ratings.md) — estimated-rating batch endpoint, per-event derivation breakdown
- [Schedule view API](backend/schedule.md) — plan-view classification normalization, response filtering
- [Recommendations](backend/recommendations.md) — Tournament Recommendation Engine, `rec_engine` crate, `/api/v3/view/recommendations`
- [Live view API](backend/live.md) — upcoming registered tournaments for the iOS Live tab, `/api/v3/view/live`
- [FencingTracker egress & caching](backend/fencingtracker.md) — process-global egress limiter/cooldown, `get_fencer` cache split
- [Internal refactor notes](backend/refactors.md) — internal refactors with no HTTP contract change

## Route Lifecycle Guidance

When introducing a backend route:

1. Add route registration through `RoutezRouter` so `/routez` stays accurate.
2. Record at least one intended caller (`web`, `mobile`, `service`, or `ops`) in docs.
3. Add/update tests for the handler behavior and auth expectations.
4. If API-facing, update the matching per-area note under [`docs/backend/`](backend/) (or a relevant product spec) in the same PR.

When deprecating/removing a backend route:

1. Mark disposition in `docs/backend-route-inventory.md` (`remove now`, `deprecate`, or `keep`).
2. Remove route wiring and the route-specific handler.
3. Remove internal functions/types that become unreachable.
4. Update docs and any client/API wrappers that referenced the removed path.
5. Verify with `cd backend && cargo build`, `bazel build //backend:backend`, and `./tools/checks run`.

## Conventions

- The `routez` crate wraps Axum's Router and tracks route metadata for introspection.
- Handler error enums map to HTTP responses through `routez`'s shared helpers rather than hand-rolled `IntoResponse` impls: `routez::error_response(status, body)` builds a `(StatusCode, message)` response, and the `routez::error_into_response!` macro generates the whole `IntoResponse` impl from a `pattern => status, message` table (with an optional `log = "..."` clause for the `tracing::error!` line). The blob crate's ~13 view/API error types (`view/fencer`, `view/fencers`, `view/registrations`, `view/ratings`, `view/recommendations`, `view/results`, `view/schedule`, `view/standings`, `family`, `invitations`, `usafencing`, `fencingtracker`, `fencingtimelive`) use this instead of repeating the same log-then-match-then-`.into_response()` boilerplate. This is a pure internal refactor: every type keeps its exact status-code and message mapping, so no route's request/response contract changes.
- String normalization has one shared, parameterized core: `util::text::normalize(input, &NormalizeOptions { .. })` (`backend/util/src/text.rs`). It walks the characters, case-folds the alphanumeric ones (`CaseFold::Upper`/`Lower`/`Keep`), turns each run of non-alphanumeric characters into a separator (`Separator::Space`/`Dash`) or drops them (`Separator::Drop`), optionally drops stopword tokens, and optionally collapses runs / trims leading-and-trailing separators. The blob crate's previously hand-rolled helpers are all thin wrappers over it, each keeping its exact prior semantics (proven by unchanged unit tests): `view::normalize_tournament_name` (lower + space + collapse + trim, `the` stopword, with its own empty-result fallback), `view::schedule::slugify` (lower + dash, preserve runs, trim), `fencingtracker::normalize_name_key` (upper + space + collapse + trim), `fencingtracker::normalize_abbreviation` (upper + drop), and `keyword_match::normalized_values`' collapsed/compact forms (lower). `view::normalize_tournament_name` remains the shared tournament-name helper for fuzzy matching, called by `view/fencer.rs`, `view/schedule/mod.rs`, and the `admintasks` crate's `{backfill_connected_fencer_results,push_results}`. All of this is a pure internal refactor with no route request/response contract change; `util::text` depends only on the standard library, with no back-edge to `blob`.
- Redis caching is handled in `blob/src/cache.rs`. To add a Redis-cached async function, use the `redis_cached!` macro (from `crate::cache`) rather than `cached`'s `#[io_cached]` attribute directly. It expands to the same runtime shape `#[io_cached]` produced — a lazily-initialized `AsyncRedisCache<K, V>` static named `FN_NAME_UPPERCASED`, a cache-checking wrapper, and a `{fn}_prime_cache` primer — but takes the key/value types and a real error-mapping closure as macro arguments instead of the string-literal `ty`/`create`/`map_error`/`convert` args `#[io_cached]` requires (which cannot be factored into a shared wrapper, since `#[io_cached]` re-parses those literals with `syn::parse_str`). The cache name (hence Redis key namespace and TTL config lookup via `create_cache`), key derivation, and cache-on-`Ok` behavior are identical to `#[io_cached]`. Optional `refresh = <bool>` selects `create_cache_with_refresh`; optional `convert = { <expr> }` overrides the default key (a clone of the function's arguments).
- External data scraping lives in domain-specific modules: `fencingtimelive/`, `fencingtracker/`, `usafencing/`.
- Embedded JSON assets (under `blob/src/assets/`) are loaded via the shared helpers on `Asset` in `blob/src/app.rs`: `Asset::load_json_or_default` (missing/unparseable asset → `T::default()`) and `Asset::load_json` (returns `Ok(None)` when absent, propagates deserialization errors). Prefer these over hand-rolling `Asset::get(...)` + `serde_json::from_slice`.
- Configuration files: `config-common.toml`, `config-secrets.toml` (not checked in).

## Logging Environment Tags

- Backend logs include an `env` field derived from `logs.server_variant`.
- Production/staging set this in `backend/production-config/prod.toml` and `backend/production-config/staging.toml`.
- Request logs and background-task logs both inherit the environment tag so logs are distinguishable in shared sinks.
```

The entry point is `backend/main.rs`. It is the composition root: it assembles a `blob::startup::Extensions` from the crates layered above `blob` (today `admintasks`) and passes it to `blob::run_sync()`, which calls into `backend/blob/src/app.rs`.

## Key Dependencies

- **Web framework:** Axum 0.8
- **Async runtime:** Tokio (multi-threaded)
- **Database:** Azure Cosmos DB (`azure_data_cosmos`)
- **Caching:** Redis via `cached` crate
- **Auth:** `jsonwebtoken`
- **Scheduling:** `tokio-cron-scheduler`
- **Observability:** `tracing` with JSON output, Prometheus metrics

## API Versioning

The API has versioned modules (`v2/`, `v3/`). New work should target `v3`.
When a PR changes backend API behavior, include a related docs update in the same PR — in this file, in the matching per-area note under [`docs/backend/`](backend/) (see [Subsystem API Notes](#subsystem-api-notes)), or in a product spec. This is a team convention, not a CI gate.

## Subsystem API Notes

Per-area backend API-surface notes live under [`docs/backend/`](backend/), one file per subsystem. They were split out of this file so it can stay a small, stable conventions doc. Backend PRs that change API behavior append notes to these files; putting every note in one growing tail of this document made concurrent PRs conflict textually. Per-area files spread those appends out so logically independent PRs stop colliding.

When you change an API's behavior, add the note to the matching area file below (or to a product spec under `docs/product-specs/`).

- [Routes & operational endpoints](backend/routes.md) — route cleanup history, operational & shim endpoints, dynamic flags, OAuth state, CORS
- [Results view API](backend/results.md) — rollout observability, connected-fencer backfill, bout-backed read-path, video API, FencingTimeLive import, manual refresh
- [Fencers view API](backend/fencers.md) — `GET /api/v3/view/fencers` follow/notify + listing
- [Standings view API](backend/standings.md) — cached enriched-view read path, connected-fencer standings endpoint
- [Ratings view API](backend/ratings.md) — estimated-rating batch endpoint, per-event derivation breakdown
- [Schedule view API](backend/schedule.md) — plan-view classification normalization, response filtering
- [Recommendations](backend/recommendations.md) — Tournament Recommendation Engine, `rec_engine` crate, `/api/v3/view/recommendations`
- [Live view API](backend/live.md) — upcoming registered tournaments for the iOS Live tab, `/api/v3/view/live`
- [FencingTracker egress & caching](backend/fencingtracker.md) — process-global egress limiter/cooldown, `get_fencer` cache split
- [Internal refactor notes](backend/refactors.md) — internal refactors with no HTTP contract change

## Route Lifecycle Guidance

When introducing a backend route:

1. Add route registration through `RoutezRouter` so `/routez` stays accurate.
2. Record at least one intended caller (`web`, `mobile`, `service`, or `ops`) in docs.
3. Add/update tests for the handler behavior and auth expectations.
4. If API-facing, update the matching per-area note under [`docs/backend/`](backend/) (or a relevant product spec) in the same PR.

When deprecating/removing a backend route:

1. Mark disposition in `docs/backend-route-inventory.md` (`remove now`, `deprecate`, or `keep`).
2. Remove route wiring and the route-specific handler.
3. Remove internal functions/types that become unreachable.
4. Update docs and any client/API wrappers that referenced the removed path.
5. Verify with `cd backend && cargo build`, `bazel build //backend:backend`, and `./tools/checks run`.

## Conventions

- The `routez` crate wraps Axum's Router and tracks route metadata for introspection.
- Handler error enums map to HTTP responses through `routez`'s shared helpers rather than hand-rolled `IntoResponse` impls: `routez::error_response(status, body)` builds a `(StatusCode, message)` response, and the `routez::error_into_response!` macro generates the whole `IntoResponse` impl from a `pattern => status, message` table (with an optional `log = "..."` clause for the `tracing::error!` line). The blob crate's ~13 view/API error types (`view/fencer`, `view/fencers`, `view/registrations`, `view/ratings`, `view/recommendations`, `view/results`, `view/schedule`, `view/standings`, `family`, `invitations`, `usafencing`, `fencingtracker`, `fencingtimelive`) use this instead of repeating the same log-then-match-then-`.into_response()` boilerplate. This is a pure internal refactor: every type keeps its exact status-code and message mapping, so no route's request/response contract changes.
- String normalization has one shared, parameterized core: `util::text::normalize(input, &NormalizeOptions { .. })` (`backend/util/src/text.rs`). It walks the characters, case-folds the alphanumeric ones (`CaseFold::Upper`/`Lower`/`Keep`), turns each run of non-alphanumeric characters into a separator (`Separator::Space`/`Dash`) or drops them (`Separator::Drop`), optionally drops stopword tokens, and optionally collapses runs / trims leading-and-trailing separators. The blob crate's previously hand-rolled helpers are all thin wrappers over it, each keeping its exact prior semantics (proven by unchanged unit tests): `view::normalize_tournament_name` (lower + space + collapse + trim, `the` stopword, with its own empty-result fallback), `view::schedule::slugify` (lower + dash, preserve runs, trim), `fencingtracker::normalize_name_key` (upper + space + collapse + trim), `fencingtracker::normalize_abbreviation` (upper + drop), and `keyword_match::normalized_values`' collapsed/compact forms (lower). `view::normalize_tournament_name` remains the shared tournament-name helper for fuzzy matching, called by `view/fencer.rs`, `view/schedule/mod.rs`, and the `admintasks` crate's `{backfill_connected_fencer_results,push_results}`. All of this is a pure internal refactor with no route request/response contract change; `util::text` depends only on the standard library, with no back-edge to `blob`.
- Redis caching is handled in `blob/src/cache.rs`. To add a Redis-cached async function, use the `redis_cached!` macro (from `crate::cache`) rather than `cached`'s `#[io_cached]` attribute directly. It expands to the same runtime shape `#[io_cached]` produced — a lazily-initialized `AsyncRedisCache<K, V>` static named `FN_NAME_UPPERCASED`, a cache-checking wrapper, and a `{fn}_prime_cache` primer — but takes the key/value types and a real error-mapping closure as macro arguments instead of the string-literal `ty`/`create`/`map_error`/`convert` args `#[io_cached]` requires (which cannot be factored into a shared wrapper, since `#[io_cached]` re-parses those literals with `syn::parse_str`). The cache name (hence Redis key namespace and TTL config lookup via `create_cache`), key derivation, and cache-on-`Ok` behavior are identical to `#[io_cached]`. Optional `refresh = <bool>` selects `create_cache_with_refresh`; optional `convert = { <expr> }` overrides the default key (a clone of the function's arguments).
- External data scraping lives in domain-specific modules: `fencingtimelive/`, `fencingtracker/`, `usafencing/`.
- Embedded JSON assets (under `blob/src/assets/`) are loaded via the shared helpers on `Asset` in `blob/src/app.rs`: `Asset::load_json_or_default` (missing/unparseable asset → `T::default()`) and `Asset::load_json` (returns `Ok(None)` when absent, propagates deserialization errors). Prefer these over hand-rolling `Asset::get(...)` + `serde_json::from_slice`.
- Configuration files: `config-common.toml`, `config-secrets.toml` (not checked in).

## Logging Environment Tags

- Backend logs include an `env` field derived from `logs.server_variant`.
- Production/staging set this in `backend/production-config/prod.toml` and `backend/production-config/staging.toml`.
- Request logs and background-task logs both inherit the environment tag so logs are distinguishable in shared sinks.
```

A fleet of replicas racing this at boot is coordinated by a short-TTL `SET NX` lock (`standings:view_cache:version_heal_lock`) rather than the version key itself, so a replica that loses the race just skips _requesting_ a sweep this boot — it never marks the bump as healed.
